business_model.claim: Verisign sells domain name registry services and critical internet infrastructure, including registration and authoritative resolution for the .com and .net top-level domains.
quotes: We are a global provider of critical internet infrastructure and domain name registry services, enabling internet navigation for many of the world’s most recognized domain names.

business_model.basis: stated in P4; retail pricing by registrars stated in P1
business_model.claim: Its direct customers are registrars, not the end registrants, who contract with registrars or their resellers.
quotes: Individual customers, called registrants, contract directly with registrars or their resellers, and the registrars, who are our direct customers, in turn register the domain names with Verisign.

business_model.claim: For .com and .net, Verisign earns a fee from registrars per annual registration, and the fee is set under its agreements with ICANN.
quotes: For domain names registered in the .com and .net registries, we receive a fee from registrars per annual registration that is determined pursuant to our agreements with ICANN.

business_model.claim: Substantially all revenue comes from operating .com and .net. Other gTLDs and one ccTLD are not significant to consolidated revenue.
quotes: Substantially all of our revenues are derived from our operation of the .com gTLD under our Cooperative Agreement with the DOC and our .com Registry Agreement as well as our operation of the .net gTLD under our .net Registry Agreement.
We also derive revenues from operating domain name registries and technical systems for several other gTLDs and one ccTLD, all of which are not significant in relation to our consolidated revenues.

business_model.claim: Revenue moves mainly with new registrations, the renewal rate of existing registrations, and price increases allowed by ICANN and the Department of Commerce.
quotes: Changes in revenues are driven largely by changes in the number of new domain name registrations and the renewal rate for existing registrations as well as the impact of new and prior price increases, to the extent permitted by ICANN and the Department of Commerce.

business_model.claim: Price increases are capped by contract: .com by up to 7% in each of the final four years of each six-year period, and .net by up to 10% each year.

Under the .net Registry Agreement, we are permitted to increase the price of .net domain name registrations by up to 10% each year during the term of our agreement with ICANN, through June 30, 2029.
